subject: chemistry
question_text: What is Boltzmann's constant? Give its value.

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. NOTATION: the book writes K = R/N; this card uses the standard symbols k_B = R/N_A with the same meaning and the same value.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Boltzmann's constant is the gas constant per
molecule: the universal gas constant R divided
k = R / N   (N = 6.022 × 10²³ molecules per mole)
steps.why: R belongs to one mole of gas. Dividing by the number of molecules in a mole gives the same constant scaled down to one molecule, and that per-molecule constant is Boltzmann's constant.
common_mistakes: Writing k = R × N instead of R divided by N.
Calling it the gas constant per mole. Per mole is R itself; per molecule is k.
steps.memory_tip: R is per mole, k is per molecule. Divide by the Avogadro number to go from mole to molecule.
steps.margin_note: The words per molecule must appear; k = R/N alone is not the definition.

steps.label: The value
lines: In CGS units: k = 1.38 × 10⁻¹⁶ erg K⁻¹ molecule⁻¹
steps.why: Dividing R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ by N = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ gives 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ for one molecule. The value is checkable, not a number to take on trust.
common_mistakes: Writing the power as 10⁻²² or 10⁻²⁴. The exponent is part of the mark.
Leaving out the unit J K⁻¹.
steps.memory_tip: 8.314 divided by 6.022 × 10²³ comes to about 1.4 × 10⁻²³. The SI value ends in ⁻²³, the CGS value in ⁻¹⁶.
steps.margin_note: The SI value in the box is enough; the erg value is extra.

insider_note: Both halves are asked by name — the definition and the value — so leaving either out gives away a full mark.
